slides.title: Social Simulations: from Agent-Based Modeling to Digital Twins
slides.highlight: This work explores the transition from agent-based modeling to LLM-enhanced simulations and Social Digital Twins, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: A survey on the evolution of social simulations from rule-based agent-based modeling to LLM-enhanced digital twins.
card.key_idea: Transitions from classical ABMs (explicit rules) to LLM-ABMs (natural language reasoning) and Social Digital Twins (data-driven, high-fidelity replicas of specific real-world socio-technical systems).
card.evaluation: Evaluated via literature survey and references to studies on opinion dynamics, persuasion, and polarization using LLM agents and network structures.
card.limitation: High sensitivity to prompt design, potential for model biases, and significant computational costs for high-fidelity digital twins.

slides.title: NeuraFrame Studio Launches Embodied AI Memory Layer
slides.tldr: EMBODIED AI MEMORY LAYER FOR ROBOTS
slides.highlight: NeuraFrame Studio has introduced a memory layer that enables robots to learn without requiring onboard AI models, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: UBTech Launches Hyper-Real Humanoid Robots for Lonely People
slides.highlight: UBTech has introduced hyper-real humanoid robots designed to assist lonely individuals, providing a relevant example of embodied social robotics for RwB.

slides.title: Analysis of Mutual and Referential Human and Robot Gazes in a Collaborative Word Association Game
slides.tldr: ROBOT GAZE IMPACT ON HUMAN ATTENTION
slides.highlight: This study examines how mutual and referential robot gazes affect human visual attention and confirmation-seeking behavior during a collaborative task, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: Robot gaze orientation does not significantly influence human visual attention during a cognitively demanding collaborative game.
card.key_idea: A NAO robot used LLM-driven dialogue in a word association game to test if mutual or referential gaze affects human fixation times and confirmation-seeking behavior.
card.evaluation: 10 non-native English speakers were tested using Tobii Glasses 3 and YOLOv8 AOI segmentation. Results showed no statistically significant effect of robot gaze on fixation.
card.limitation: Small sample size (N=10) and potential cognitive load from non-native language use may have skewed results.

slides.title: Requirement-Driven Design of Whole-Body Social Tactile Sensing via Virtual Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework to derive tactile sensing requirements from interaction data, supporting the development of social robots capable of recognizing human touch gestures.

card.one_liner: A framework using VR to derive robot tactile sensor placement and resolution requirements before hardware fabrication.
card.key_idea: VR-based interaction data allows offline reconstruction of contact geometry, enabling simulation of various sensor layouts and resolutions to optimize gesture recognition accuracy without physical prototypes.
card.evaluation: Tested on 18 participants with 5,520 trials across 8 gestures. Used Random Forest and CNN-GRU classifiers with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.
card.limitation: Simulation uses binary contact signals only (no force/pressure) and was evaluated exclusively on a single robot's arm.

slides.title: Breaking the 15% Barrier: A Real-World Data-Driven System for Proactive Social Robot Triggered by User Nonverbal Cues
slides.highlight: This research develops a dialogue framework that uses nonverbal cues and vision-language models to enable proactive robot responses, supporting RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A real-time system enabling social robots to proactively initiate dialogue based on user nonverbal cues.
card.key_idea: A multi-label recognizer using V-JEPA2 and a ViT-based architecture detects nine key behaviors, which are then fed as tokens into an LLM for behavior-conditioned utterance generation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation (0.8 micro-F1) and offline intent agreement (49.1%) against teleoperator data from a 6-day real-world retail deployment.
card.limitation: Low accuracy for rare task-related directives and limited generalization due to data from a single store entrance.

slides.title: Forgetting Our Way to Shared Meaning: Effects of Forgetting on Conceptual Alignment in a Non-Partnership Coordination Game
slides.tldr: IMPACT OF MEMORY DEGRADATION ON CONCEPTUAL ALIGNMENT
slides.highlight: This research explores how memory characteristics and adaptiveness influence the emergence of shared meaning in non-partnership coordination games, providing insights for the agent models used in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Adaptive memory improves actual conceptual alignment but leads agents to underestimate their shared meaning.
card.key_idea: A non-partnership coordination game using Voronoi tessellations to model conceptual regions, comparing adaptive agents with non-adaptive agents experiencing memory degradation.
card.evaluation: Counterfactual simulations with varying prototypes (3-10), adaptiveness (1-10%), and degradation rates. Results show adaptive players converge faster and more closely.
card.limitation: Simulations use fixed deliberative strategies and do not currently account for complex network structures or endogenous agent interactions.

slides.title: CF-Net: Conflict Fusion with Speaker Normalisation and Certainty Weighting for Ambivalence/Hesitancy Recognition
slides.highlight: CF-Net utilizes cross-modal incongruence and speaker normalization to detect ambivalence and hesitancy, supporting HyECHO's goals in multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: CF-Net recognizes ambivalence and hesitancy by explicitly modeling cross-modal incongruence using frozen multimodal backbones.
card.key_idea: Combines per-speaker normalization, a ConflictFusion module (pairwise absolute-difference features), and certainty-weighted focal loss with an auxiliary regression head to handle annotation ambiguity and speaker identity leakage.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the BAH dataset; achieved 0.7155 Macro F1 (validation) and 0.7364 (private test), outperforming several prior challenge baselines.
card.limitation: Uses frozen backbones; the authors suggest selective fine-tuning or learned cross-modal attention could further improve performance.

slides.title: Real-time Generation of Listener Nodding via Prediction of Kinematic Parameters for Avatar Dialogue Systems
slides.highlight: This research proposes a model for real-time prediction of nodding timing and kinematic parameters, contributing to HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement in human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: A real-time model predicting both the timing and kinematic parameters of listener nodding for conversational avatars.
card.key_idea: Dyadic attention networks using Continuous Mimi Encoders predict nodding onset and kinematic parameters (range, speed, repetitions, swing-up), with the parameter module fine-tuned from the timing module.
card.evaluation: Five-fold cross-validation on 90 dialogues and subjective evaluation (n=60) showed significant improvements over stochastic and fixed-motion baselines in naturalness and attentiveness.
card.limitation: Subjective evaluations were conducted via pre-recorded videos as third-party observers rather than through direct, face-to-face interactions.

slides.title: ERR@HRI 3.0 Challenge: Multimodal Detection of Errors and Anticipation in Human-Robot Interactions
slides.highlight: This work introduces datasets for detecting bystander reactions and anticipatory facial responses to robot failures, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction quality.

card.one_liner: ERR@HRI 3.0 introduces datasets for multimodal detection and anticipation of errors in human-robot interactions.
card.key_idea: Two raw video datasets (BAD and Bad Idea) enable end-to-end multimodal ML models to detect bystander reactions and anticipate failure outcomes in naturalistic settings.
card.evaluation: Three teams submitted models that were compared against CNN baselines using raw, crowdsourced video data from 45 and 29 participants.

slides.title: A Glimpse into Long-term Physical Coexistence with Intelligent Robots
slides.tldr: MULTI-ROBOT AGENT ARCHITECTURE FOR LONG-TERM COEXISTENCE
slides.highlight: The paper introduces PHILIA, a multi-robot agent designed for long-term physical coexistence through a unified capability interface. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots by enabling compositional user experiences and grounding agent memory in robot actions.

card.one_liner: PHILIA is a multi-robot architecture decoupling high-level agent reasoning from low-level physical robot execution.
card.key_idea: A robot gateway abstraction exposes a unified capability interface, allowing a central control plane to coordinate heterogeneous robots via semantic reasoning and long-term memory.
card.evaluation: Tested on Astribot S1 robots and a 483-utterance dataset across 7 LLMs; frontier models achieved 89–94% skill matching accuracy.

slides.title: MafiaScope: Non-Invasive, Time-Resolved Belief Probing for LLM Agents in Social Deduction Games
slides.tldr: BELIEF PROBING FOR LLM AGENTS IN SOCIAL DEDUCTION
slides.highlight: MafiaScope provides a testbed for measuring machine Theory of Mind in social deduction games, which supports MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models in societal-scale simulations.

card.one_liner: MafiaScope is an open testbed for measuring LLM Theory of Mind via non-invasive belief probing.
card.key_idea: Agents are privately questioned after every utterance using a YAML-defined probe engine; answers are scored against ground truth without influencing the game's persistent context.
card.evaluation: Case study of 32 DeepSeek games (13,815 answers) and a 30-fork replay experiment. Results show poor confidence calibration and over-prediction of being suspected.
card.limitation: Probe answers are self-reports that may be unfaithful, and the replay experiment used a small sample size (N=5 per arm).

slides.title: Validating Virtual Reality for Studying Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction in Socially Aware Robot Navigation
slides.tldr: VR VALIDATED FOR SOCIAL ROBOT NAVIGATION STUDY
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that VR can reliably capture multimodal interaction dynamics and perceived social awareness in human-robot co-navigation, supporting the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: VR is validated as a reliable platform for studying multimodal human-robot interaction in socially aware navigation.
card.key_idea: A VR prototype replicating a real-world arena was used to compare human locomotion trajectories and head-orientation cues during co-navigation with a PR2 robot.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects study (N=21) using orthogonal crossing and pass-by scenarios. Evaluated via 5-point Likert scales, trajectory analysis, and head-orientation metrics; results showed consistent behavioral patterns.
card.limitation: Lack of auditory cues, restricted headset field-of-view, and reduced naturalness of locomotion compared to real-world walking.

slides.title: A New Human-Likeness and Comfort Index for Robot Movements Along Prescribed Paths
slides.tldr: NEW INDEX FOR HUMAN-LIKE ROBOT MOVEMENT COMFORT
slides.highlight: This research introduces a human-likeness index based on the lognormality principle to evaluate robot trajectory comfort, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A new quantitative index evaluates robot movement comfort by measuring similarity to human-like motor programs.
card.key_idea: The Human-Likeness (HL) index combines the Signal-to-Noise Ratio of a sigma-lognormal velocity reconstruction with a penalty for the number of strokes used to model the movement.
card.evaluation: Validated with 68 subjects across three experimental campaigns; results showed a consistent trend between perceived comfort and the calculated HL index.
card.limitation: The index may not capture human-like movements involving additional strokes generated by spinal cord signals based on proprioceptive information.
